lines.text: /* One file, no network. Colors come from the host's theme variables when it has them
(T3 Code sets them on an inline page), else from the system colors, so the page
follows light and dark with no theme of its own. */
/* Opened on its own, the page needs the gutter a host frame would give it. */
/* Words both sides share step back, so the eye lands on what differs. */
/* The answer a card already holds, shown when you step back to it. */
// The page builder replaces this value with the round: { id, duels, ideas, webhook }.
// Half the duels show y first. The answer is stored as x or y, never as a side of the screen.
// One answer per card: a second tap waits for the next card, and that card waits a moment
// too, because the second tap of a double-tap lands on it.
// In two near-equal texts, the words both hold step back. Texts that differ more read whole.
card.append(el("div", "eyebrow", open ? open + " left open" : "all answered"));
card.append(el("h1", "", "Paste this code in the thread."));
// One send per code, so a reload or a second look at this screen sends nothing new.
const sent = el("p", "hint", "Sending it to your agent…");
// A plain text POST needs no preflight, so it also leaves a sandboxed frame.
() => (sent.textContent = "Sent to your agent. The code above is a spare."),
() => (sent.textContent = "Could not send it. Paste the code instead."),
